# **My Work On Nomenclatura Porta**

# Overview

Nomenclatura Porta is a Chemistry elements/symbols practice application for University Of Toronto Schools (UTS). 

# My Contributions

I was tasked with improving the frontend along with adding many new features, and I was also tasked with creating a brand new backend implementing GraphQL and migrating all existing restapi endpoints from the previous backend into a GraphQL query/mutation.

Old UI (Only has One Page):

# Technical Overview

with a Blazor Web frontend, and a [ASP.NET](http://ASP.NET) Core backend. The backend uses a SQL Server database along with EF Core and GraphQL, while the frontend uses Blazor along with MudBlazor.

# Backend

![][image1]  
The Image above shows the directory structure of the backend [ASP.NET](http://ASP.NET) Core Web project. It exposes a GraphQL endpoint at “/” and a Rest Endpoint at “/restapi/Auth”.

| *“/”* | Queries/Mutations |
| :---- | :---- |
| ***“/restapi/Auth/Authenticate”*** | **Provides Database User lookup and Windows Authentication** |

The backend uses HotChocolate as its GraphQL library of choice, along with Entity Framework Core paired with SQL Server. Below is a full list of all NuGet Packages being used:  
![][image2]

Using dependency injection, a preconfigured EF Core service is made available to all classes that may require access to the SQL Server.   
![][image3]  
This prevents the creation and disposing of multiple instances of DBContext after each request. Instead each class stores one instance and reuses it. This saves resources and is mildly faster. 

## GraphQL Implementation

After accessing the endpoint, the server needs to be able to give the frontend access to a number of queries/mutations. The developer has to write the logic behind each query/mutation that they may need.  
***A Simple Query Logic:***  
![][image4]  
Most queries are under 10 lines of code, and so a developer can write all implementation logic in the same file and keep it looking nice and tidy.

However, mutations are much longer and so, I have abstracted implementation logic in another file called   
***A Simple Mutation:***  
HotChocolate for .NET comes packaged with ChilliCream Nitro, and this allows for easy query/mutation building and testing.
